records.rationale: Retain the optional all-CPU backtrace module parameter for the configured generic DPM watchdog. The full single-file patch adds only the parameter/include and fatal-time diagnostic call. Default false remains, current read uses READ_ONCE, and native fatal panic/stack capture remains. This is a source/runtime diagnostic control, not historical KMI. No SDK script setting it was established; retain conservatively with the current configured interface.

Retain both privileged timeout sysctls with the original validation and compile-time upper bound. Adapt consumption in 1cea64c5f402: each armed watchdog samples timeout and warning with READ_ONCE and caps warning to its sampled timeout. Its handler uses those stable values, preventing later updates from extending the deadline or making unsigned remaining-time subtraction underflow. Concurrent writers/global pairs are not made atomic; the effective per-watchdog pair is normalized and immutable after publication. Native two-stage warning/panic and synchronous timer cleanup remain.

Retain the complete MODULE_PARAM_PREFIX rename to pm. This establishes the current pm.dpm_watchdog_enabled and backtrace parameter names for Android boot/runtime source compatibility; do not preserve the old generated file-based prefix as a binary interface. No new writable mode or privilege is added by this two-directive change.

All three paths reviewed: retain DPM_WATCHDOG_ENABLED Kconfig, boot/runtime enable parameter, and matching kernel-parameter documentation. Current SDK builds DPM watchdog but disables it by default; preserve that Android configuration. Correct the original independent set/clear checks by storing enabled in each stack instance before any early return, so false-to-true cannot destroy an uninitialized timer and true-to-false cannot leave a timer pointing to returned stack storage. Runtime changes affect subsequent instances; documentation records this deliberate safe lifecycle behavior. Existing native timer_delete_sync/destroy and callback ordering remain; no running PM/timer verification.

security: The original writable enable flag is sampled twice independently around a stack-owned timer. A change between set and clear can either skip timer cleanup or touch an uninitialized timer. Keep a per-instance enabled decision and native synchronous delete/destroy. Stable per-instance timeout values also prevent live changes from invalidating the two-stage deadline; warning is capped to timeout because independent global reads may observe different updates. Existing sysctl permission 0644, positive lower bounds and CONFIG_DPM_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT upper bound stay. Default disabling is an Android availability/diagnostic policy: a hung device callback may lack this panic/capture mechanism until enabled. This does not remove native suspend authorization or an LTS memory-safety fix. Retain native driver/task lifetime through the set/clear interval. No actual kernel timer, panic or sysctl race test.
uncertainty: No SDK consumer of the writable watchdog knobs was established in scoped system/frameworks/goldfish searches. Retain the configured generic Android runtime/module control conservatively. Global sysctl writer operations are not serialized with each other: the normalized per-instance pair makes consumption bounded, not globally transactional. Runtime changes deliberately affect subsequent watchdog instances; no immediate cancellation of an armed watchdog is promised.
